edges.note: MVP is an alternative interactive-UI decomposition derived from the MVC lineage; presenter replaces controller+observer sync.
MVVM binds view to a view-model via data binding; MVP wires a presenter with explicit calls - competing UI mediation styles.
Both decompose an interactive app; MVVM uses declarative binding to a view-model instead of controller-driven change propagation.
MVVM is Gossman/Microsoft's WPF-tailored specialization of Fowler's toolkit-independent Presentation Model.
PM holds all view state in a self-sync class; Passive-View MVP puts that logic in a presenter - alternative placements.
MVU (immutable model + pure update/view) is an alternative to MVC's mutable model with controller-mediated updates.
Both are unidirectional data-flow UI architectures; Flux/Redux explicitly credit the Elm Architecture as inspiration.
MVI recasts Elm's model-update-view cycle over reactive streams (intents); sibling unidirectional UI structures.
MVI's reactive intent-to-state cycle competes with MVVM's binding-to-view-model as the app's UI structure.
PAC structures a hierarchy of PAC agents as an alternative to MVC for interactive systems; POSA1 relates the two.
The two principal ways to organize domain logic: one procedure per transaction vs an interconnected object model.
Both organize domain logic procedurally; Transaction Script per request, Table Module one class per table.
One class per table (record-set oriented) vs a rich per-object domain model - the two OO domain-logic options.
Service Layer defines system operations that coordinate an underlying Domain Model (domain-facade style).

edges.cite: Fowler, PoEAA, Service Layer / Remote Facade
edges.note: A Service Layer's coarse operations are commonly exposed remotely via a Remote Facade.
In its operation-script variant a Service Layer implements each operation as a Transaction-Script-like procedure.
A Bounded Context is the boundary within which one Domain Model and its ubiquitous language stay consistent.
A Context Map documents the relationships between the several Bounded Contexts of a large system.
An Anti-Corruption Layer shields one Bounded Context's model from another's when they must integrate.
Giving each service its own database lets each pick the store best suited to its needs - polyglot persistence.
Multiple specialized stores per need vs one shared database serving all - opposing data-management strategies.
A dedicated reporting store is one of the specialized datastores a polyglot-persistence system deliberately runs.
Reporting databases are typically populated as precomputed materialized views of the operational data.
A separate reporting store realizes the read side of CQRS, offloading queries from the operational write model.

edges.cite: Microsoft Azure Architecture: Materialized View / CQRS patterns
edges.note: CQRS read models are commonly built as materialized views refreshed from the write store.

edges.cite: Microsoft Azure Architecture: Strangler Fig pattern
edges.note: During incremental migration the new system talks to the legacy through an Anti-Corruption Layer.

edges.cite: Microsoft Azure Architecture: Strangler Fig pattern
edges.note: A routing facade intercepts requests and redirects them between legacy and new implementations as they migrate.

edges.cite: Douglass, Real-Time Design Patterns (Layered Pattern family)
edges.note: A concrete five-layer template (app/UI/comm/abstract-OS/abstract-hardware) is a specialization of the Layers style.
Its lowest (abstract-hardware) layer is a Hardware Abstraction Layer making upper layers portable.
A HAL is a dedicated bottom layer in a firmware layering; it is a specialization of the Layers style.
A BSP supplies the board-specific driver/config implementations that realize the HAL interfaces for a given board.
A BSP bundles the board's boot code and clock/pin init that the boot-stage architecture runs at startup.
The pattern layers a concurrent system into synchronous, queueing, and asynchronous layers - a Layers specialization.
SEDA generalizes the sync/async split into a graph of queue-separated stages; same buffered-handoff idea.
Lower controllers in the hierarchy execute local feedback control loops carrying out goals set from above.
Recursive Control (Selic) is a uniform recursive form of control hierarchy: every component pairs functional+control parts.
Recursive control parts are applied at each level of the recursively contained subsystem structure.
Recursive subsystem containment provides the nested structure over which a control hierarchy is distributed.
A tiered processor chain (always-on front end feeding larger downstream stages) is a hardware pipeline of stages.
The small always-on processor wakes/feeds downstream processors on detected events - event-triggered handoff.
Both are top-level structures for tiny MCUs: swap one whole executable at a time vs a single continuous superloop.
Switching between independent single-application executables requires a boot/load stage to select and start one.
The fault-tolerance variant dispatches identical work to replicated slaves and reconciles their results.
The master can vote on/compare slave results to mask a faulty slave or improve accuracy.
Both spread work over a worker pool; master pushes partitioned tasks vs consumers pulling from a shared queue.
MapReduce is a data-parallel master-worker: a master assigns map/reduce tasks to a pool of identical workers.
Supervisors apply restart strategies and escalate failures up the tree when local restarts exhaust their limits.
Each supervisor is the designated component in charge of seeing its children's failures through to recovery.
Each supervised worker/subtree is a recovery granule - the unit within which errors are contained and restarted.

edges.cite: Hanmer, Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software (Heterogeneous vs Homogeneous Redundancy)
edges.note: Diverse (design-diverse) redundancy vs identical copies - opposing redundancy strategies for different fault classes.
Diversely designed channels must produce the same output for the same input, so their results are voted/compared.

edges.cite: Hanmer, Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software; IEC 61508
edges.note: TMR is a specific triplicated form of identical (homogeneous) redundancy with majority voting.
TMR is the 2oo3 case of the MooN channel-voting family.
A majority voter forwards the agreed result of the three channels, masking any single channel failure.
2oo3 majority masking (fail-operational) vs 1oo2 cycle-by-cycle comparison (fail-safe) - different redundancy topologies.
MooN channels feed a voter that acts when M of N channels agree/demand.
Comparators check the two cycle-aligned cores every cycle and flag a fault on any divergence.
A Safety Executive coordinates fail-safe transitions triggered by Monitor-Actuator detection channels.
The independent monitor compares the actuator's physical effect against setpoints and forces fail-safe on divergence.
The Safety Executive relies on watchdogs as a liveness-detection input to its fail-safe coordination.
The Safety Executive is the identified component in charge of all safety shutdown/recovery decisions.
The watchdog receives periodic liveness (heartbeat) evidence and triggers recovery when it stops arriving.
ARINC 653 Health Monitor detects/recovers faults at process, partition, and module levels of the partitioned RTOS.
Configured multi-level recovery escalates from process restart to partition restart to module action.

edges.cite: Hanmer, Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software (Architectural patterns)
edges.note: Someone in Charge acts within/over the Units of Mitigation that bound error containment and recovery.

edges.cite: Hanmer, Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software
edges.note: The Fault Observer reports faults that the designated Someone-in-Charge then drives to resolution.

edges.cite: Hanmer, Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software
edges.note: Faults detected within Units of Mitigation are surfaced through the Fault Observer to the rest of the system.
A Unit of Mitigation is the recovery granule that aligns with a fault-containment region bounding error spread.
OS-enforced partitions act as fault-containment regions: a partition cannot affect another's memory or timing.
IMA hosts multiple avionics applications on shared hardware using robust time-and-space partitioning.
Both give hardware-enforced isolation of software components: many fixed partitions vs a two-world secure enclave.

edges.cite: Schumacher et al., Security Patterns (Authentication + Authorization)
edges.note: SSO establishes authenticated identity; Authorization then decides which actions that subject may perform.
Cross-domain SSO is realized by federating identity so one authentication is trusted across independent systems.
SSO is a concrete topology realizing the Authenticate Actors security tactic across many systems at once.
Authorization decisions are enforced at guarded access points - the PEP consulting a PDP against the policy.
The Authorization pattern is a concrete subject-object-rights structure realizing the Authorize Actors tactic.

edges.cite: Provos et al., 'Preventing Privilege Escalation' (OpenSSH privsep)
edges.note: The unprivileged worker processes are run sandboxed so a compromise cannot reach privileged operations.
A TEE is hardware-enforced privilege separation: a small secure world exposes a narrow interface to the rich OS.
A sandbox isolates an instance from the real world, restricting its access to real resources - a Limit Access form.
One-directory, one-header components with acyclic dependencies is a concrete component-based organization.
Dependencies may point only toward more fundamental components - an explicit restrict-dependencies rule.
